payload.title: TI P4-04: Threat Intelligence publication repo scaffold on the packages (brand, theme, infra/site.json)
payload.description:
## Goal
Make the app-shell template able to put the site on https://threat-intelligence.anth.us (a host under the shared root domain anth.us) and give it a staging host that does not collide with Anth.us. Smallest change that works; none if the existing form already suffices.

## Context (FACT)
- Old app d3on1y5vlrxmam has ONE domain association: domainName anth.us, subdomain prefix threat-intelligence on branch main, status AVAILABLE; Route 53 zone Z02552332GG6AM25SFP73 (anth.us) has threat-intelligence.anth.us CNAME to a CloudFront domain. App d2hbn1ig6nqyhy (Anth.us live) ALSO holds a domain association on anth.us (prefixes include www): the same root domain is associated with two apps in this account today.
- The template (infra/amplify-app-shell/lib/amplify-app-shell.ts) creates AWS::Amplify::Domain with domainName = cms.domainName and subDomainSettings [{ branchName: main, prefix: "" }], and requires hostedZoneId when a domain is set. It cannot express root domain anth.us with prefix threat-intelligence, and whether Amplify accepts domainName "threat-intelligence.anth.us" as its own domain while anth.us is associated with other apps is UNVERIFIED.
- resolveStagingDomainName (lib/site-config.ts) derives the staging host by replacing the first label of cms.domainName with staging: threat-intelligence.anth.us would give staging.anth.us, the Anth.us staging name. cms.stagingDomainName overrides it.
- Pretext: the public site and /newsroom are one app, so cms.domainName is the PUBLIC host here (the Pretext example uses newsroom.example.test; for TI it is the public name).

## Exact steps
1. Gherkin: scenario "a site under a shared root domain gets a domain association for the root with its own prefix" and "staging host is explicit when the CMS host is under a shared root".
2. Decide by reading the CloudFormation AWS::Amplify::Domain docs and a cdk synth diff: if domainName "threat-intelligence.anth.us" with prefix "" is valid for a subdomain whose root is shared, no code change; otherwise add optional cms.domainPrefix (root domain stays in cms.domainName) with validation and docs. Do not add a collision validator (YAGNI); document that cms.stagingDomainName must be set explicitly when cms.domainName is under a shared root.
3. Add examples/threat-intelligence.site.json (no secrets) and update the README section on domains.
4. Unit/synth tests: the synthesized template contains the expected CfnDomain properties for TI's site.json.

## Acceptance checks
- Template tests green; cdk synth of examples/threat-intelligence.site.json shows the Domain and StagingDomain resources with the expected names and prefixes.
- The ticket records which form was chosen and the evidence; the live proof happens in P4-11.

## Rollback
Close the PR.

## Risks
The real behavior (can a second app claim a prefix on a root already associated with another app, and with the old TI app still holding its association) can only be proven with an AWS write; P4-11 does that with a rollback.

## Needs Ryan
PR review and merge only.

## Common rules (Phase 4 Threat Intelligence)
- Plan and facts: the assessment comment on the Phase 4 ticket (PPY-332889). Pattern: docs/migrations/pilobol-us.md and docs/standard-site.md 3.2 on origin/develop.
- Ryan: Threat Intelligence is PRE-PRODUCTION; goal is to dogfood the new backend CMS UX before converting anth.us (production). Treat as a hard cutover with brief downtime accepted unless Ryan says otherwise (open question Q1). The OLD app d3on1y5vlrxmam and its backend stay untouched and serving until the retire ticket.
- Read AGENTS.local.md first. AWS_PROFILE=legacy, us-east-1 (SSO is Ryan's). Never print env var or secret VALUES (names only). Never run ampx pipeline-deploy locally. Creating, changing or deleting AWS resources needs Ryan's explicit yes in chat for that step; deleting data or stacks is done by Ryan or on his explicit yes. Read-only AWS calls are fine.
- NEVER use /Users/home/Projects/Pilobol.us as a build dir. TI repo work: fresh clone under /Users/home/Projects/ (delete afterwards), feature branch + PR, never push to its main. Papyrus repo: worktree of origin/develop under /Users/home/Projects/Papyrus-worktrees/, branch feature/PPY-<id>-<slug>, PR into develop, never merge to main, never git stash, trailer Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>, PR body ends with the Claude Code generated-with line. In /Users/home/Projects/Papyrus (the board checkout) only run kbs; never git add or commit there.
- Gherkin first for any Papyrus behavior change (AGENTS.md). Long clear names, no line-level comments.
- Update this ticket with branch, PR link and command output when done.
